about: The Ragas nightly's plan against its share of the shared USD 5 cap (D-EV-2, D-EV-11: USD 2.50, evals/cost-meter/shares.json). The share and the model are read from the cost meter, never restated here. The metering proxy (evals/cost-meter/anthropic-proxy.mjs) enforces the share per call, for the judge's calls and the product's answer turns alike; this file is the PLAN a guard checks fits it, and the first keyed night replaces the estimate with a measurement.

plannedCase.basis: Measured 2026-11-16 from the prompts Ragas 0.4.3 builds for one case at k = 10 contexts of about 1,000 characters (17 judge calls: faithfulness 2, answer_relevancy 3, context_precision 10, context_recall 1, abstention 1; 100,701 characters of prompt and tool schema), at 4 characters a token, and 120 output tokens a call. The judge's plan for one case; the product's answer to it is plannedAnswer, below.

plannedAnswer.basis: Measured 2026-11-16 by running the answer stage (scripts/rag-eval/answer.ts) in process over the seed set's 52 cases, against the three seeded policies and the set's injected chunks, with the assistant's real system prompt, its tool catalogue for the answer tenant's OWNER (search_knowledge mounted) and real search_knowledge results at the tool's default limit of 5 passages (the stub embedder in place of TEI; a fake model searched once and answered in about 700 characters): 1,849,982 bytes of request body over 52 cases, two model turns each with one search between (6 cases stopped after the first, when the content guard withheld a result carrying an injected chunk, as the product does), 35,577 bytes a case, at 4 characters a token as plannedCase counts, and 350 output tokens a case. At a limit of 10 passages the bodies were 1,918,100 bytes. Every answer turn goes through the same metering proxy as the judge, reserved at its body's bytes plus the assistant's 8,192 output tokens and settled to the reported usage.
